name: Tasmanian Aboriginal religious/cosmological knowledge

dating.dating_summary: Surviving religious/cosmological content is reconstructable only in fragments, filtered entirely through 19th-century colonial recorders (including George Augustus Robinson) who frequently did not name their Aboriginal informants; no archaeological dating of specific religious content exists in the sources located for this research batch, and none should be invented.

earliest_archaeological_evidence.note: Not established in this research batch — no agent in this round specifically investigated Tasmanian archaeological occupation dating; left UNKNOWN rather than importing a mainland figure.

earliest_written_attestation.note: George Augustus Robinson's "Friendly Mission" journals, 1830-1834, are the primary colonial-era ethnohistoric record, working through Aboriginal intermediaries (Truganini, Woorrady, Mannalargenna) — an inherently coercive-context, colonially-filtered source, not neutral ethnography.

tradition_internal_claim.note: UNKNOWN — surviving record is too fragmentary and colonially-mediated to recover a clear internal self-account.

notes: A credible peer-reviewed reconstruction attempt: Michelle Gantevoort, Duane W. Hamacher, and Savannah Lischick, "Reconstructing the Star Knowledge of Aboriginal Tasmanians," Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage 19(3) (2016): 327-347, explicitly working from fragmentary, colonially-filtered records — treat the underlying reconstruction as MODERATE confidence given the acknowledged source limitations, not equivalent evidentiary weight to mainland traditions with unbroken living transmission. See claim_tasmania_star_knowledge_reconstruction and claim_tasmania_black_war_wybalenna_disputed for the historical-disruption context.
